correctness.rationale: The final theorem quantifies genuine continuous copulas Cφ(u,v)=uv[u+(1−u)φ(v)] with φ differentiable in (0,1), φ≤1, vφ(v)→0 at zero, φ+vφ′≥0, vφ′≤1, and mandatory continuity at v=1 with φ→1. Since vφ is nondecreasing from 0, φ≥0; integrating φ′≤1/v to the upper endpoint gives φ(v)≥max(0,1+ln v). With D(v)=v(1−φ(v)), the Spearman rho is −2∫D(v)dv and its infimum is −(1−e^{−2})/2≈−0.432332358381694. Equality would force φ=max(0,1+ln v) identically, whose kink at e^{-1} violates interior differentiability, so lower endpoint unattained. Density c(u,v)=1−(1−2u)D′(v) is nonnegative under the two derivative bounds; integration by parts with D(0)=D(1)=0 gives Kendall tau=−4/3∫D=(2/3)rho. The explicit soft-maximum φ_ε(v)=ε ln[1+(e^{1/ε}−1)v^{1/ε}] is smooth and admissible for ε>0, approaches the kink as ε↓0, and approaches φ≡1 as ε→∞; continuity in ε fills the entire open-lower/closed-upper segment. Independent symbolic checks and high-precision integration corroborate constants and limiting family, but unrestricted conclusion follows analytically.
